messages.subject: InformativeTesting with 'control' variables
parts:
Hi everyone,

I am have a specific issue with the InformativeTesting function when testing order constraints in a LGC model with an exogenous ‘control’ variable.

I am helping write a pre-registration where the authors plan to fit a LGC model with an exogenous continuous control variable (household income) and a categorical grouping variable (perceived relative income inequality; PRIE). They want to test whether a certain category of the categorical grouping variable (those who perceive themselves as poorer) does ‘worse’ than the other categories, which is why I am fitting a LGC model with order constraints.

I simulated some data where the order constraints are clearly true/present, however I am having trouble with the InformativeTesting function. In short, the InformativeTesting function successfully identifies the order constraints being present in the data when I do not include the exogenous ‘control’ variable in the model (Type A test p < 0.05; Type B test p > 0.05); however, once I include the exogenous ‘control' variable in the model the function produces a result that there are not order constraints present (Type A test p > 0.05; Type B test p > 0.05). This even occurs if I simulate the data in such a way that there is no correlation between the exogenous ‘control’ variable and the categorical variable which is used for the order constraints. 

As there are no examples online of the InformativeTesting function used with control variables in the model, I am unsure whether the issue I am experiencing is because the function is not designed to be used on such models? 

I have added a toy example below. Any help/pointers would be greatly appreciated.

Best wishes,
Amy 

## Toy example of Informative.Testing issue
### Orben, Amy; 16.09.2020
## This is an example to show how the informative.testing function ceases to pick up a order constraint in simulated data
## when an exogenous 'control' variable is added. 
## For a pre-registration I am hoping to test for order constraints in a model with multiple 'control' variables
## so I need to address this issue. Further, if there is a way to constrain the parameters of the 'control' variables
## (e.g. income in this toy example) to be equal for the categorical variable used to test the order constraints
## I would love to know! 

library(lavaan) 
library(tidyverse) 

# Simulate data

## simulate LCS model data with two exogenous variables (income and perceived relative income inequality)
set.seed(1234)
simulate_model <-'
x_2 ~ 1*x_1     
dx =~ 1*x_2     
x_2 ~ 0*1         
x_2 ~~ 0*x_2    

dx ~ -1*1        # This fixes the intercept of the change score
x_1 ~ 10*1       # This fixes the intercept of x_1

dx ~~ 2*dx    # This fixes the variance of the change score
x_1 ~~ 3*x_1  # This fixes the variance of the x_1

dx~0*x_1   # This fixes the self-feedback parameter to 0. 

###### We now add the two exogenous variables
### household income (income) and perceived relative income inequality (prie)
x_1 ~ 0.05*income
dx ~ 0*income
income ~~ 0.2*income
income ~ 5.9*1

x_1 ~ -0.4*prie
dx ~ -0.9*prie
prie ~~ 0.3*prie
prie ~ 1.5*1

prie ~~ -0.2*income
'

## Simulate data
simdat<-simulateData(simulate_model, sample.nobs = 1000, meanstructure = T)

## Make PRIE into a categorical variables with three levels
simdat$prie <- cut_number(simdat$prie, 3, labels = c("rich", "same", "poor")) 

# Order Constraints Testing
## We create two models, one without the exogenous control variable and one with the exogenous control variables

## Create model without exogenous 'control' variable (income)
model_withoutincome <- '
x_2 ~ 1*x_1    
dx =~ 1*x_2     
x_2 ~ 0*1        
x_2 ~~ 0*x_2   

dx ~ c(c_p,c_s,c_r)*1       
x_1 ~ c(i_p,i_s,i_r)*1         
dx ~~ dx  
x_1 ~~ x_1      
dx ~ x_1  
'

## create model with exogenous 'control' variable (income)
model_withincome <- '
x_2 ~ 1*x_1    
dx =~ 1*x_2     
x_2 ~ 0*1        
x_2 ~~ 0*x_2   

dx ~ c(c_p,c_s,c_r)*1       
x_1 ~ c(i_p,i_s,i_r)*1         
dx ~~ dx  
x_1 ~~ x_1      
dx ~ x_1  

dx ~ income            
x_1 ~ income      
income ~~ income
income ~ 1
'

## specify constraints
constraints <- '
c_p < c_r
c_p < c_s

i_p < i_r
i_p < i_s
'

## run informative testing on both models
test_withoutincome <- InformativeTesting(model = model_withoutincome, data = simdat, 
                                               constraints = constraints,
                                               double.bootstrap = "no",
                                               R = 10, group = "prie", 
                                               parallel = "multicore", ncpus = 8)
test_withincome <- InformativeTesting(model = model_withincome, data = simdat, 
                                            constraints = constraints,
                                            double.bootstrap = "no",
                                            R = 10, group = "prie", 
                                            parallel = "multicore", ncpus = 8)
# Results

## the model that does not include the exogenous control variable succeeds in picking up the simulated order constraints
test_withoutincome

## the model that includes the exogenous control variable however fails in doing so
test_withincome

## Note: the problem persists if I simulate data without a correlation between income and prie

Thank you so much - that worked! I didn't know you could simulate multiple groups in the simulateData function, so I am glad I learnt this today. 

I copied the working code below for those interested.

## Toy example of Informative.Testing issue
### Orben, Amy; 16.09.2020
## This is an example to show how the informative.testing function ceases to pick up a order constraint in simulated data
## when an exogenous 'control' variable is added. 
## For a pre-registration I am hoping to test for order constraints in a model with multiple 'control' variables
## so I need to address this issue. Further, if there is a way to constrain the parameters of the 'control' variables
## (e.g. income in this toy example) to be equal for the categorical variable used to test the order constraints
## I would love to know!

## simulate LCS model data with two exogenous variables (income and perceived relative income inequality)
set.seed(1234)
simulate_model <-'
x_2 ~ 1*x_1     
dx =~ 1*x_2     
x_2 ~ 0*1         
x_2 ~~ 0*x_2

dx ~ c(-1.5,-1.2,-1)*1        # This fixes the intercept of the change score
x_1 ~ c(8,10,12)*1       # This fixes the intercept of x_1

dx ~~ 2*dx    # This fixes the variance of the change score
x_1 ~~ 3*x_1  # This fixes the variance of the x_1

dx~0*x_1   # This fixes the self-feedback parameter to 0. 

###### We now add the two exogenous variables
### household income (income) and perceived relative income inequality (prie)
x_1 ~ 0.05*income
dx ~ 0*income
income ~~ 0.2*income

income ~ c(4.5,5.9,6.1)*1
'

## Simulate data
simdat<-simulateData(simulate_model, sample.nobs = c(3300,3300,3300), meanstructure = T, group.label=c('poor','same','rich'))
simdat$group <- dplyr::recode(simdat$group, `1` = "poor", `2` = "same", `3` = "rich")

# Order Constraints Testing
## We create two models, one without the exogenous control variable and one with the exogenous control variables

## Create model without exogenous 'control' variable (income)
model_withoutincome <- '
x_2 ~ 1*x_1    
dx =~ 1*x_2     
x_2 ~ 0*1        
x_2 ~~ 0*x_2   

dx ~ c(c_p,c_s,c_r)*1       
x_1 ~ c(i_p,i_s,i_r)*1         
dx ~~ dx  
x_1 ~~ x_1      
dx ~ x_1  
'

## create model with exogenous 'control' variable (income)

x_2 ~ 1*x_1    
dx =~ 1*x_2     
x_2 ~ 0*1        
x_2 ~~ 0*x_2   

dx ~ c(c_p,c_s,c_r)*1       
x_1 ~ c(i_p,i_s,i_r)*1         
dx ~~ dx  
x_1 ~~ x_1      
dx ~ x_1  

dx ~ income            
x_1 ~ income      
income ~~ income
income ~ 1
'

## specify constraints
constraints <- '
c_p < c_r
c_p < c_s

i_p < i_r
i_p < i_s
'

## run informative testing on both models
test_withoutincome <- InformativeTesting(model = model_withoutincome, data = simdat, 
                                               constraints = constraints,
                                               double.bootstrap = "no",

parallel = "multicore", ncpus = 8)
test_withincome <- InformativeTesting(model = model_withincome, data = simdat, 
                                            constraints = constraints,
                                            double.bootstrap = "no",
